ELI5: how does music affect our mood?

I'm not an expert or anything, but here's just my ballpark educated guess. There are these things called neurotransmitters in our brains that affect how we think and feel and do stuff. Different neurotransmitters do different things. The neurotransmitters that are responsible for mood fire off when listening to music, kinda making us feel some way. But I think it has a lot to do with vibrations as well as things that can affect us just musically--like hearing something unexpected, or creating dissonance/tension, an epic buildup and resolve, etc.. But it is all subjective. One person could love the sound of electronic music and it could pump them up, and another person could just hear it as annoying noise. So I think culture/peers also have a big affect on how we perceive music and how we let it affect us. So while our neurotransmitters ultimately have the affect on our mood, how those neurotransmitters are fired off depends a lot on environmental factors. I hope someone else can chime in and shed some more light on this.

Oh no, heavy storage that is used frequently is still from regular WDD drives. I do use another WDD drive for some games, but all of those files are easily obtainable if the drive fails.

Heavy storage used frequently gets a mechanical drive, because cost. Any storage used infrequently gets a mechanical drive, because retention period. SSDs are for anything you frequently access that isn't very big (or the speed outweighs the cost).
